sources.note: Institution history: Alfonso X 1273; stockowners, rights of passage/grazing and exemptions.

sources.title: University of Salamanca: History

sources.title: Archdiocese of Oviedo heritage: San Julián de los Prados
sources.note: Information: Alfonso II 791 to 842, Roman/Visigothic reused pieces, frescoes, exterior-only chamber of uncertain function; modern restoration 1912 to 1915.

sources.title: Archdiocese of Oviedo heritage: Foncalada
sources.note: Information: uncertain dating, spring/channel/basin, Christian inscriptions and ritual water symbolism.

sources.title: Archdiocese of Oviedo heritage: Santa María del Naranco
sources.note: Ramiro I 842 to 850; complex; lower room linked tentatively to bathing; vaulted upper hall; altar 848 mentions Ramiro and Paterna.

sources.title: Oviedo Cathedral: Cámara Santa
sources.note: Cross of Angels 808; gold/wood, reused Roman engraved gems; angel-makers presented as legend; Cross of Victory 908 and Agate Box 910.

sources.title: José Julio Martín Barba: La Cruz de Oviedo, Universidad Complutense
sources.note: Cross of Angels 808; Latin inscription HOC SIGNO TVETVR PIVS; royal legitimacy and later repetition.

sources.title: UNESCO: Decreta of León 1188
sources.note: Memory of the World entry: elected town representatives in royal assembly alongside church, nobility and king.

sources.title: UNESCO nomination: Decreta of León
sources.note: Pages 2 to 3 history and content; justice, legal procedure, witnesses, sealed summons; record transmitted in originals and later copies. Intro contains obvious date typos not reproduced.

sources.title: Museo de San Isidoro: El Palacio
sources.note: Mid 11 c Fernando/Sancha palace; 12 c Sancha Raimúndez chamber/oratory; later scriptorium; reused Roman wall tower.

sources.title: Museo Arqueológico Nacional: Crucifix of Ferdinand and Sancha
sources.note: Ivory crucifix, donated 1063, figures, hidden relic cavity and portable/displayed function.

sources.title: Museo Arqueológico Nacional: Tesoros singulares, Crucifijo
sources.note: Object sheet 2018: inscription FREDINANDVS REX/SANCIA REGINA; probable Leonese workshop, donation 1063.

sources.title: Biblioteca Nacional de España: Beatus of Ferdinand and Sancha
sources.note: VITR 14/2, 1047, 317 parchment leaves, 98 miniatures; probable Facundus workshop attribution; original Beatus lost.

sources.title: Museo de San Isidoro: El Panteón de los Reyes
sources.note: Museum interpretation sheet: 11 c royal burial portico; New Testament frescoes, annunciation to shepherds depicted through medieval pastoral life.

sources.title: PARES: Petronila of Aragon
sources.note: Biography: 1137 betrothal pact, 1150 marriage to Ramon Berenguer IV, Alfonso II; distinction between child betrothal and later wedding.

sources.title: Government of Aragon Virtual Library: Crown of Aragon
sources.note: Authority note: 1137 transfer to count without royal title, composite crown, territorial privileges and later Nueva Planta. This library authority record explicitly incorporates Wikipedia text; it is a secondary compilation, not an independent archival source.

sources.title: Getty Museum: Masterpieces, Illuminated Manuscripts
sources.note: Entry 22, Vidal Mayor, MsLudwigXIV 6, c 1290 to 1310; 1247 commission, Navarro-Aragonese translation of lost Latin, legal cases across religious/status groups.

sources.title: MUHBA: Merda urbana/BCN, Manel Guàrdia, 2022
sources.note: Page 1, medieval sections: 1303 street-cleaning ordinance, private latrines/chamberpots and sewage works 1364 to 1366. Later 18 to 19 c practices excluded.

sources.title: MUHBA: Barcelona, capital mediterránea
sources.note: Page 49: six hospitals merged 1401, municipal/church support, poor/orphans/sick; food supply and social policy.

sources.title: University of Valencia: Llibre de Sent Soví
sources.note: 2021 presentation: medieval recipe collection in miscellany with medical, grammatical, astrological and devotional texts; facsimile/transcription.

sources.title: PARES: Council of Aragon
sources.note: Institutional history: created 1494, regional secretariats, suppressed 1707.

sources.title: RAE/BOE legal historical dictionary: Nueva Planta decree
sources.note: First decree 29 June 1707 affects kingdoms of Aragon and Valencia; historical institutional change.

sources.title: Parliament of Navarre: Nuestra historia
sources.note: History sections: Pamplona/Navarre origins, 1512 invasion, 1515 annexation, continuing institutions until 19 c.

sources.title: Eusko Ikaskuntza: La conquista de Navarra
sources.note: Historical synthesis: conquest 1512 to 1529, UpperNavarre 1515, LowerNavarre 1620, continued kingdom status.

sources.title: Royal and General Archive of Navarre: Fuero General exhibition
sources.note: 13 ccompilation, Navarro-Aragonese, gradual judicial authority; 14 cCodex A1 black/red ink includes 1330 amendment.

sources.title: Municipality of Olite: Royal Palace
sources.note: Charles III 1387 to 1425 andEleanor; named master builders, water raised by buckets/leadpipes, gardens and menagerie. Luxury court evidence, not ordinary households.

sources.title: Roncesvalles municipality: History
sources.note: 12 csection: 1127 care brotherhood, 1134 political separation and 1135 institutional expansion; land/rent gifts supported hospital.

sources.title: Royal Archive of Navarre: Caminar a Santiago
sources.note: Exhibited urban charters 1122/1129 andBecerro deIrache hospital privilege; later 1563 hospitalconstitutions not used for medieval claims.

sources.title: Archive of Navarre Library: Machín de Zalba letter
sources.note: Two undated letters probably 1416 on same support; Basque andNavarreseRomance, tax reduction and dinner plans; jaunatiçula egun hon translation.

sources.title: Alhambra Patronato: History
sources.note: 13th to 15th-century section: 1238 court, urban refugees, Yusuf I/Muhammad V; post 1492 royal residence andMorisco artisans.

sources.title: Alhambra Patronato: Gardens, the miracle born of water
sources.note: Muhammad I 1238, fortified city, Acequia Real, agricultural almuniaGeneralife; continued gardens after 1492.

sources.title: Alhambra Museum: El ajuar de la casa nazarí
sources.note: 2015 exhibition: keys, lamps, braziers, basins/chamberpots, cooking location, spindlewhorls/thimbles. Source generalizes toilets to every home; card deliberately limits claim to represented material evidence.

sources.note: 2017 museum study: claywhistles, miniaturevessels, animal/humanfigures; Nasrid and laterChristian dates explicitly distinguished.

sources.title: Alhambra Patronato: History of the Maristán
sources.note: Origin section: poor Muslim patients, Muhammad V, foundationinscription 1365 to 1367; earlier building reused; post 1499 to 1502 mint.

sources.note: 1349 to 1492 section: Madrasa Yusufiyya, legal/religious subjects, Arabic, astronomy/calculation/geometry, resident students andendowment; laterfunctiondecline.

sources.note: Nasrid motto inArabic andSpanish; tilewithshieldmuseumexample; Kufic/cursive distinction and palace inscriptions.

sources.note: Timeline: 1238 Granadacapital; CatholicMonarchsenter 2 January 1492.

León 1000–1279 remains separately drawn past union 1230. Its own card explicitly identifies the historical union and leaves polygon chronology unverified.
